context: Treemap of 27 D3 skill files grouped into 8 categories, with area proportional to line count. Uses a Tol muted palette with per-category color headers and intra-category lightness variation to distinguish siblings.
first_impression: The category labels are readable but the leaf cells are nearly invisible — dark-on-dark rendering makes the treemap body a field of near-black rectangles with no discernible content.
what_works: Category grouping is structurally clear: colored header labels at each group boundary let the viewer orient to the 8 sections at a glance. The 8-color Tol palette is a good choice — colorblind-safe and perceptually spaced.
what_doesnt: The intra-category lightness variation fails catastrophically: applying `darker(0.8)` to already-dark hues like #332288 produces near-black fills, and `brighter(0.3)` is not enough to recover contrast against the dark background — most cells are indistinguishable from each other and from the background. Leaf labels are almost entirely unreadable: the conditional rendering (w>50, h>28) suppresses labels for small cells, and the white text on near-black fill blends away for the rest, so the viewer cannot identify individual skills without hovering every cell.
